newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 12.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:

** The Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment cleared Videsh Sanchar Nigam's $750 million global depositary receipts issue on Tuesday. It also approved the proposal of Hindustan Petro Chemicals for a joint venture with Total of France to set up a liquefied natural gas terminal, the Economic Times reports.
A proposal for an increase in foreign equity

participation in Tata Teleservices' project by Bell Canada to 49 percent was also approved. Among other approvals were Fiat's four-wheeler joint venture with the Doshi's, owners of Premier Automobiles and Daewoo's proposal for increasing stake in its joint venture with DCM to 49 percent, the paper says.

** An unfavourable outlook given to India's sovereign rating by Moody's Investors Service Inc was unlikely to have any immediate impact on either foreign inflows or the cost of India's external borrowings, bankers and analysts said on Tuesday.
They also questioned whether Moody's report took into
account policy measures announced in the federal budget on February 28, which have been favorably received by Indian financial markets.
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.845/855 against the dollar on Wednesday, almost unchanged from the previous close, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is seen defending the
dollar by buying the U.S. currency from the spot or forward markets, they said.
** Indian shares closed sharply lower on Tuesday as investors booked profits after seeing the market struggle to make further headway, traders said.
They said foreign funds were likely to turn bidders at
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange shed 42.87 points, or 1.1 percent, to close at 3725.87.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 26.70 points, or 2.5 percent, to 1,052.0.
** The Delhi share index was down 7.80 points, to 786.36.
